name: Big Two
description: Big Two (also known as Choh Dai Di or Pusoy Dos) is the quintessential Chinese climbing card game. It features a unique ranking hierarchy where the 2 is the most powerful card and the 3 is the weakest. Players compete to empty their hands by playing increasingly higher combinations of cards, including singles, pairs, and standard five-card poker hands. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to manage their high cards (deuces) while clearing their weaker low cards through tactical passing and control of the lead.

content.text: Big Two (also known as Choh Dai Di or Pusoy Dos) is the quintessential Chinese climbing card game. It features a unique ranking hierarchy where the 2 is the most powerful card and the 3 is the weakest. Players compete to empty their hands by playing increasingly higher combinations of cards, including singles, pairs, and standard five-card poker hands. The game is highly strategic, requiring players to manage their high cards (deuces) while clearing their weaker low cards through tactical passing and control of the lead.

Emerging in coastal China (likely Shanghai or Hong Kong) in the mid-20th century, Big Two combined the climbing mechanics of traditional Chinese games with the globally recognized ranking of poker hands.
Deal the entire deck clockwise (13 cards to each player). The player holding the 3 of Diamonds leads the first trick.

items.text: Pusoy Dos (Philippines): Standard rules but often uses a different suit hierarchy (Diamonds high).
Taiwanese Big Two: Allows 'Dragon' sequences (13 cards) and has different multipliers for 2s left in hand.
